summary: Formalized a comprehensive architectural governance framework using AST-based analysis, the Cognitive Complexity Sentinel (CCS), and the Architectural Drift Sentinel (ADS) to quantify health and enforce domain-driven design. This system treats technical debt as a first-class entity, utilizes a Compliance Scoring Engine to ensure alignment with strategic directives, and maintains a strict complexity budget to prevent structural drift.
key_learnings: AST-based parsing and structural hashing provide the most reliable defense against state-space ambiguity.
Cognitive complexity is a superior proxy for maintainability compared to cyclomatic complexity.
Quantifying architectural health via DCS and churn-complexity correlation provides a predictive risk profile.
Technical debt must be treated as a first-class entity with a quantifiable lifecycle.
Refactoring ROI is maximized by targeting the intersection of high cognitive complexity and high version control churn.
Automated governance via a centralized naming schema and Tree-sitter validation reduces cognitive load.
Quantifying alignment requires a weighted framework to distinguish between mandatory directives and strategic suggestions.
The 'Justification Gap' is best closed by mandating a rationale for all rejected or modified architectural suggestions.
Materiality thresholds are essential to prevent compliance fatigue.
Integrating architectural health metrics directly into the self-check loop prevents the accumulation of technical debt during autonomous cycles.
